Photo by Kelly Sikkema on Unsplash“Clean Architecture is too complicated.”
I’ve heard this statement countless times.
Some developers avoid it because they think it’s only for enterprise applications.
Others believe it requires creating hundreds of files before writing a single feature.
And some simply give up after looking at one of those intimidating architecture diagrams filled with circles, arrows, and unfamiliar terminology.
The irony?
You’ve probably already been using parts of Clean Architecture without realizing it.
Because at its core, Clean Architecture isn’t about following a rigid set of rules.
It’s about keeping responsibilities organized.
Nothing more.
In this chapter of the Flutter Architecture Masterclass, let’s remove the mystery surrounding Clean Architecture and understand what it really is — and what it isn’t.
The Name Makes It Sound More Complicated Than It Is
When people hear “Clean Architecture,” they often imagine something like this:

• Entities

• Use Cases

• Repositories
